desc:
You have n computers and a set of batteries; battery i can power one computer for batteries[i] minutes in total. Each computer needs exactly one battery connected at every minute it runs. At any whole minute you may disconnect any batteries and connect others, as often as you like and instantly; a battery can be moved between computers and used in several separate stretches, but never powers two computers in the same minute, and it stops working once its charge is used up. You are given at least n batteries.

Return the largest integer T such that all n computers can run simultaneously for T minutes.

Example: n = 2, batteries = [3, 3, 3]. Total charge 9 allows at most 4 minutes for two computers. Rotating the batteries gives exactly 4 minutes, so the answer is 4.
hints: Ask the yes/no question for a target T: can all computers run for T minutes? Total charge needed is n * T.
A single battery can never contribute more than T minutes to the target, however large its charge. So its useful charge is min(b, T).
It turns out that T is achievable exactly when sum(min(b, T)) ≥ n * T. This is monotone in T, so binary search T between 0 and sum(batteries) // n.
editorial: For a target T, each battery can supply at most T minutes, because during the T minutes it can power only one computer at a time. So the usable supply is sum(min(b, T)), and we need n * T minutes of power in total. The condition sum(min(b, T)) ≥ n * T is necessary. It is also sufficient: lay the T minutes of all computers out as a long line of n * T slots and fill batteries into it one after another, each battery taking at most T consecutive slots; a battery never wraps onto the same computer's minute twice because its length is at most T.

The condition is monotone: as T grows, the left side grows by at most one per battery that is still unsaturated, while the right side grows by n. Since at least n batteries exist, once it fails it keeps failing. Binary search in O(m log(sum / n)) time with O(1) extra space, where m is the number of batteries. A greedy that keeps the n - 1 largest batteries as dedicated and averages the rest also works.
